messages:
molly: Ran nightly eval after upgrading to model-v3.9-2026-03-18-weights + int8 quant. Hit a 5x spike in the 'bad_generation' alert on promptset `legalqa`. samples look truncated and oddly repetitive. Any ideas? :eyes:

rajiv: saw that. dashboard shows spike starting ~02:10 UTC. p99 latency is flat, CPU/GPU utilization normal. accuracy down, repetition up.

molly: pasting a couple of clipped samples below. first float16 (baseline), then int8.

molly: ```
--- float16 (v3.9 unquantized) ---
Q: When does the statute of limitations run out for contract disputes?
A: Typically, statutes vary by jurisdiction, but the common rule is X years from the breach date or discovery of the breach. Exceptions apply for fraud or tolling.
--- int8 (v3.9 int8-static) ---
Q: When does the statute of limitations run out for contract disputes?
A: The the the the the statute of limitations is is is governed governed governed by by by ...
```

jeff: can you paste exact model+commit and tokenizer sha? also which quant pipeline used?

molly: model: `model-v3.9-2026-03-18-weights`
quant: `int8-static` (calibration run on nightly corpus)
tokenizer: `tokenizer-v2.0.4`

tara: heads-up: tokenizer-v2.0.4 changed merging rules for ellipses and several dash/emdash mappings compared to v2.0.3. That can shift token boundaries.

rajiv: if token boundaries moved, KV cache offsets can get misaligned and produce repetition or truncation when prefixing is involved.

molly: reproducer command: `./eval/run_eval --promptset legalqa --model model-v3.9-2026-03-18-weights:int8-static --seed 42 --save-samples out.json`

ci-bot: nightly-eval: job 8742 completed. report: https://nightly.redwood/8742/index.html ; artifacts at s3://redwood-nightly/8742/reports/html

jeff: please run the same job against float16 unquantized weights (same tokenizer) to isolate quant impact.

molly: ran float16 locally: still a small drop but much less severe. int8 shows -12% on our automated QA metric, float16 -3%.

luis: sounds like quant calibration assumed old tokenization. We should re-run calibration with tokenizer-v2.0.4 or pin the tokenizer to v2.0.3 during quant.

tara: also try conversion with `--preserve-tokenization` (this flags-preserve certain merge ops) and see if outputs realign.

rajiv: quick log grep for kv warnings: `grep -i "kv_offset" /var/log/infer/*` — any hits?

molly: looked through canary logs, no explicit kv_offset warnings, but there is a startup line: `warning: tokenization-compatibility: tokenizer v2.0.4 != model embedding table tokenization v2.0.3`

jeff: schedule a canary rollback of the weights to v3.8 on a tiny percent of traffic for Dedicated pool while we triage. suppress noisy alert for that promptset for now. :shipit:

luis: I'll re-run quant calibration (int8-static) with pinned tokenizer-v2.0.4 and also run a cross-eval: 
`calib --model model-v3.9 --tokenizer tokenizer-v2.0.4 --data sample_corpus --out calib-v3.9-tok2.0.4.cb`
Then regenerate the nightly subset. ETA ~2h.

tara: tagging product and eng-oncall to keep them in the loop, but not a security issue.

molly: thanks — I'll upload the failing sample set and link to the nightly report in the triage ticket. Reproducer + command included above.

jeff: one more check: run the eval with `--force-detokenize-check` to make any tokenization mismatches surface as warnings in logs.

molly: done, attached logs to the ticket. will report back with calibrated int8 runs.

luis: if calibration fixes it, we should add a preflight test in model onboarding: quant-calibrate-with-current-tokenizer. file an infra PR?

molly: +1. creating the triage ticket now. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
